Consider the picture above. Given that $h=\lambda f+\mu g$, find $\lambda $ and $\mu .$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251995/assets/9905448ad59cb2f68f5def832811eb34056305d1a535f23387f4403a340cb8f8.png)

In $△OFH$ shown above, we have 

- $OF=\frac{1}{2}|f|$

- $\overset{\to }{OF}$ has the opposite direction to $f$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OF}=-\frac{1}{2}f.$

Similarly:

- $FH=2|g|$

- $\overset{\to }{FH}$ has the opposite direction to $g$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{FH}=-2g.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}h & =\overset{\to }{OF}+\overset{\to }{FH} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}f-2g.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $h=\lambda f+\mu g=-\frac{1}{2}f-2g.$

Since $f∦g,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =-\frac{1}{2}$ and $\mu =-2$
